messages:
Sam K: Quick idea — instead of proliferating long-lived API keys for service-to-service calls, what if we standardize on short-lived signed attestations (think: 5m JWT-like blobs) issued by a lightweight attestation service?
Priya R: Curious, what's the main win over ephemeral API keys + rotation? :thinking:
Sam K: fewer secrets to store+rotate, easier telemetry (attestation contains caller metadata), and a clear migration path: attestation service can mint on behalf of existing API keys during transition.
Marta L: Concern: how do we prevent replay and constrain scope? signing alone isn't enough.
Jared P: add nonce+aud claim + short TTL. And require TLS mutual for sensitive hops. TTL=5m, nonce replay window checked by receiver.
Priya R: From RBAC side: we still need per-route/role scoping. Are we putting role claims into the attestation token?
Sam K: yes — include minimal claims: actor_id, actor_type (svc/user), roles[], org_id, project_id, exp, aud. Keep it intentionally small.
Marta L: How about trust boundaries? if Dedicated customers run private infra, they may want an HSM-signed attestation or a local CA.
Sam K: allow pluggable signing backends: root signing key in KMS/HSM for Redwood-hosted; for Private/Dedicated, customer-provided CA or rotating local keys. Document fallback: if signature verification fails, receiver can check via introspection endpoint (slower).
Jared P: SDK impact: add helpers to mint/refresh attestation and to inject headers. We should standardize header: `Authorization: Attest <base64>` or `X-Redwood-Attest: <token>`?
Priya R: prefer `Authorization: Attest ...` so proxies and LB rules can match easily.
Sam K: Agreed. sample header and minimal token structure:
```
Authorization: Attest eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkF0dGVzdCJ9.eyJhdWQiOiJzZXJ2aWNlLWFwaSIsImFjdG9yIjoiU1ZDLXBheW1lbnRzIiwiZmY..."

Sam K: truncated for brevity
```
Marta L: Telemetry question: do receivers log the full token? probably not. We should log the actor_id, org_id, roles, and token_id (opaque) only.
Jared P: Good call. Also add an incremental audit entry when a token is minted — who requested it, reason, and parent credential if any. That helps rollback investigations.
Priya R: Migration path: many internal services still use API keys stored in vault. We can have attestation service accept an API key to mint a short attestation for that caller for a configurable window. That avoids immediate rotation.
Sam K: Right. Two-phase: 1) Attest-on-behalf (compat), 2) Encourage callers to mint directly with service account credentials, 3) Deprecate long-lived API keys after telemetry and opt-in.
Marta L: Policy engine: receivers should consult a central RBAC service for fine-grained checks (route-level) but token claims can short-circuit obvious denials (org mismatch, expired). TTL small to limit drift.
Jared P: Edge case: background jobs with no interactive lifecycle — how do they refresh? allow long-lived service credentials stored in Vault used only to fetch attestations (not used directly for requests).
Sam K: We'll document recommended pattern: vault-stored service principal -> short-lived attest on boot -> refresh loop.
Priya R: Security checklist for RFC: signature algs and key rotation, attestor auth when minting, nonce/replay protections, header conventions, telemetry and logging rules, migration playbook.
Sam K: I'll draft a small follow-up RFC with those sections and a rough SDK prototype. Anyone want to co-author? @Priya R @Marta L
Priya R: I'll help with RBAC/telemetry sections. :+1:
Marta L: I'll take signing/backends + private deployment notes.
Jared P: I'll add SDK/ops patterns and a sample helm chart for the attestation-agent.
auth-bot: deploy-check: attestation-service:latest passed smoke tests at 1716001300 :white_check_mark:
Sam K: awesome, thanks. I'll kick off the RFC doc and link here when ready.
